analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and a new section at head lines 4816-4826 on GPT-OSS decode command-buffer commit cadence. The supplied units (head lines 420-1216) are unchanged surrounding text for context, covering Nemotron Super and GLM5Next serving, the prefix cache, admission, and the encrypted SSD checkpoint store.

Security-relevant assessment: the added text describes a performance tuning (commit a Metal command buffer every 100 operations with no input-size bound for plain decode steps) and states that results do not depend on the partitioning and that prefill keeps MLX defaults. It makes no change to code, authorization, attestation, encryption, cache scoping, TTL, or key handling. No threat-model assumptions are invalidated. T-041 (prefix-cache TTFT oracle and at-rest artifacts) and TB-007 are not affected; the docs in the units restate existing cache-scope, durable-checkpoint and memory-admission behavior without new claims that contradict the canonical threat model.

Remaining question: the actual source change (GPTOSSDecodeCommandBuffers, CBv2DecodeCommandBufferLimitsProviding) is not in the supplied evidence, so the availability and memory implications of the less frequent commits, such as GPU memory retention during longer command buffers under T-029 and T-010-style DoS concerns, cannot be verified here. The docs-only diff gives no evidence of a regression, and no finding is raised.
